# Richard Astbury's Blog

> Articles by Richard Astbury about software engineering, cloud architecture,
> AI, mapping, Microsoft Azure, and developer tools.

Canonical website: https://richorama.github.io/
RSS feed: https://richorama.github.io/feed.xml
Sitemap: https://richorama.github.io/sitemap.xml
Detailed agent index: https://richorama.github.io/agents.md

## Posts

- [Building a Conversational Alexa Skill with Microsoft Foundry Agents](https://richorama.github.io/markdown/2026-08-06-alexa-foundry.md): A practical walkthrough for connecting an Alexa custom skill to a Microsoft Foundry agent using Azure Functions, managed identity, conversational context, and a latency-safe fallback.
- [The Universe's Source Code Might Be Written in Octonions](https://richorama.github.io/markdown/2026-06-03-universes-source-code-octonions.md): An experiment in AI-assisted theoretical physics. What happens if you point a generative AI at one of the hardest unsolved problems in fundamental physics? The result is a framework with zero free parameters and 23 quantitative predictions — all matching experiment to 0.1–7%.
- [Finding New Worlds - Using Python and Open Data to Discover an Exoplanet Candidate](https://richorama.github.io/markdown/2026-01-05-exoplanets.md): How we used Python, NASA's Kepler data, and systematic validation to detect KIC 8554498 b—a potential new exoplanet with an extraordinarily strong signal that may have been overlooked. A story of open science, technical challenges, and the power of accessible astronomy tools.
- [Microsoft Copilot Researcher Solves Today's Wordle Using "Computing Using Agent"](https://richorama.github.io/markdown/2025-10-27-copilot-researcher-wordle.md): I watched Microsoft Copilot Researcher tackle today's Wordle puzzle using its "Computing Using Agent" feature. Here's how AI approaches word puzzles with systematic reasoning and computational strategy.
- [AI Self-Portraits](https://richorama.github.io/markdown/2025-07-21-ai-self-portraits.md): I asked various AI language models to create self-portraits of themselves. Here are the interesting and creative results from Gemini, ChatGPT, Copilot, and Grok.
- [Microsoft Tooling for Application Modernisation](https://richorama.github.io/markdown/2024-02-09-azure-modernisation-tooling.md): Microsoft provide various tooling options for application modernisation. Whether you are working with ASP.NET or Java, Microsoft provides a range of tools to help you discover, containerise, and migrate your applications to Azure
- [2023 Reading List](https://richorama.github.io/markdown/2023-12-31-reading-list.md): A compilation of the books I have listened to or read in 2023. I started listening to audiobooks while doing household tasks and during commutes. The standout book for the author was 'Shoe Dog' by Phil Knight, the story of the founding of Nike, which received a five-star rating.
- [Connecting Azure Logic Apps to Azure OpenAI](https://richorama.github.io/markdown/2023-12-21-logic-apps-openai.md): GenAI can also be used in a variety of ways to support 'back end' processes. Azure Logic Apps provides a great way to implement business process, with it's rich set of connectors and visual workflow designer. This guide talks through a simple example of a Logic App that calls the Azure OpenAI API.
- [Build your own Copilot](https://richorama.github.io/markdown/2023-08-08-build-your-own-copilot.md): There are many use cases for generative AI, but one that many people have been excited about is the ability to build a chatbot that can answer questions about any topic. In this post I cover the different levels of sophistication you can build into your chatbot, and how you can use the Azure OpenAI API to build your own Copilot.
- [ChatGPT Tips and Tricks](https://richorama.github.io/markdown/2023-06-14-chatgpt-tips-and-tricks.md): The ChatGPT interface is much more flexible than the chat, text generation and summarisation examples often cited. As a developer there are a few interesting use cases I have played with briefly. Here are a few examples.
- [GitHub Copilot Tips and Tricks](https://richorama.github.io/markdown/2023-06-02-github-copilot-tips-and-tricks.md): Some tips and tricks for using GitHub Copilot in VSCode
- [App Modernisation](https://richorama.github.io/markdown/2023-05-22-app-modernisation.md): Modernisation is a journey. It's the continuous acknowledgement that technical debt should be paid down, and that we should be constantly looking for ways to improve our software, and opportunities to make the team more efficient. This could include refactoring, rearchitecting, or rewriting, but it could also include improving the way we work, or the tools we use.
- [SFTP in Azure](https://richorama.github.io/markdown/2022-03-28-sftp-in-azure.md): Azure Blob Storage now provides the ability to connect to a Container using SFTP.
- [Hello Orleans 4.0](https://richorama.github.io/markdown/2022-03-22-orleans-4.md): With the advent of .NET 6, C# 10 and Orleans 4.0 (preview) it seems like a great time to take a fresh look at Microsoft Orleans.
- [Azure Blob Storage Index Tags](https://richorama.github.io/markdown/2021-08-09-azure-blob-index-tags.md): Index tags allow you to provide up to 10 key-value pairs for a blob. The tags are indexed, and you can use them to query blobs in your storage account.
- [Cryptocurrency Mining in Azure](https://richorama.github.io/markdown/2021-06-18-crypto-currency-mining-in-azure.md): I thought I would try my hand at mining crypto in the cloud. After all, who wouldn't want to be a bitcoin billionaire?
- [Offline maps with vector tiles](https://richorama.github.io/markdown/2021-01-28-offline-vector-tiles.md): On a recent project we wanted to have high quality mapping, but completely offline.
- [Adventures in Installing your own Security Camera](https://richorama.github.io/markdown/2020-11-14-sec-cam-adventures.md): I bought a £50 security camera off Amazon to improve security at our home.
- [Command Driven Map](https://richorama.github.io/markdown/2020-11-13-command-driven-map.md): I have found an approach that works well when building web based map applications in React.js. I've found in the past that map components can get very complicated very quickly making the map control hard to maintain and hard to add new features to.
- [Keeping it Simple](https://richorama.github.io/markdown/2020-10-19-keeping-it-simple.md): I recently worked on an internal project with a team of grads and inexperienced developers. Five of us in total. It was a short project - a line-of-business application to convert spreadsheets into software. It was a lot of fun.

- [Azure Maps Data Service - First Impressions](https://richorama.github.io/markdown/2019-07-04-azure-maps-data-service.md): Azure Maps consists of a set of geospatial REST APIs and a JavaScript web map control. Some of the services (including the data service) are in preview.
- [Roll your own Vector Tile service](https://richorama.github.io/markdown/2019-02-05-roll-your-own-vector-tile-service.md): Vector Tiles are an efficient way of displaying a large amount of data on a mapping control. This post we build a simple vector tile server using node. The server will generate mapping tiles on the fly, and return them to the browser as protobuf encoded vector tiles.
- [Rendering leaflet.js tiles in the browser](https://richorama.github.io/markdown/2018-08-22-rendering-leaflet-tiles-in-the-browser.md): I wrote a fractral viewer using Leaflet.js which renders map tiles in the browser using a pool of service workers.
- [Lego House](https://richorama.github.io/markdown/2018-05-01-lego-house.md): On a recent family trip to Denmark we spent a day at the Lego House in Billund. It's set back behind the Lego theme park, and has only been open for about a year.
- [Dev East](https://richorama.github.io/markdown/2018-02-12-dev-east.md): Dev East is a single day, single track software developer conference running on 16th March 2018 at Ipswich Town Football Club.
- [Bulk inserting data into SQL Server](https://richorama.github.io/markdown/2017-11-28-sql-bulk-copy.md): Let's say with have a simple table in SQL Server in which we want to insert thousands of values (Guids) from a .NET application.

So the process of getting started is now a little different. Let's walk through setting up a grain, with a silo host and client application.

- [Optimistic Concurrency in Orleans](https://richorama.github.io/markdown/2015-01-22-optimistic-concurrency-in-orleans.md): the Storage Provider infrastructure in Orleans exposes an 'Etag' field representing a particular revision of the data in the underlying storage system. This can be used to detect writes competing writes to overwrite grain state.
- [Thoughts on Deploying Orleans](https://richorama.github.io/markdown/2015-01-13-thoughts-on-deploying-orleans.md): A post discussing a future possibility for deploying Orleans to Azure
- [Running io.js on Azure Websites](https://richorama.github.io/markdown/2015-01-12-iojs-on-azure-websites.md): You can run io.js on Azure Websites easily, by configuring azure to use a custom node version. This blog shows you how.
- [Grain placement in Orleans](https://richorama.github.io/markdown/2015-01-02-grain-placement-in-orleans.md): It is possible to change this behavior by adding an attribute from the `Orleans.Placement` namespace to the Grain interface.
- [Bootstrap provider in Orleans](https://richorama.github.io/markdown/2015-01-02-bootstrap-providers-in-orleans.md): The bootstrap provider enables you to hook in some code at silo startup. There are a variety of reasons for doing this, perhaps you want to set some local grains up, or initialize some data. The Hub design pattern makes use of the bootstrap provider create a stateless worker in each Silo.
